subject: PocketPay: post-call TCO playbook and next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Alan Chu <alan.chu@pocketpay.com>, Samantha Reyes <samantha.reyes@pocketpay.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: PocketPay: post-call TCO playbook and next steps

Thanks again for a productive call this morning — quick recap and clear next steps so we stay aligned. I focused this summary on the cost/TCO levers we discussed.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- Token spend is the primary cost pressure: ~12M monthly tokens today for customer support summaries, forecasted to grow 3-4x by Q3 next year.
- Latency constraints on agent workflows: 95th pct target is 800ms end-to-end, spikes when multiple agents run sequentially.
- Budget gate: finance has a hard cap for pilot spend (~$40k over 3 months) unless we can demonstrate >3x unit ROI.

Goals from your side:
1) Run a 6-week pilot with a representative subset (50k monthly active conversations) to measure token economics and latency under realistic load.
2) Identify batching/caching opportunities to reduce per-response tokens by 20-35% and median latency by 15-25%.
3) Produce an ROI brief to take to finance with concrete savings scenarios.

TCO levers we propose (aligned to call):
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and user context: expected 10-25% token reduction on summary flows.
- Aggressive client-side batching at your aggregator layer for low-latency windows + Redwood autoscaling windows for heavy tails.
- Model selection + quantized variants for background tasks (rerank/embedding) to cut inference unit cost ~30%.
- Prompt engineering + structured outputs to lower token fan-out in multi-agent chains.

Immediate deliverables (what I'll send by EOD tomorrow):
- Redwood_TCO_Workbook.xlsx: two scenarios (conservative / aggressive) with per-token assumptions, batching impact, and pilot spend plan.
- pilot-scope-pocketpay.pdf: short one-pager outlining test payloads, success criteria, and required instrumentation (tracing + token-level cost reports).
- pricing-deck-summary.pdf: summary of committed capacity and dedicated pilot pricing options that could fit under your $40k pilot constraint.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) You confirm the pilot cohort size and a small sample of request traces (we need 2-3 days of anonymized logs).
2) I'll share the workbook and recommended config; we set a 30-min sync next Tue to walk the numbers.
3) If numbers look good, we toggle pilot procurement (terms + SOW) and schedule infra onboarding.

Questions I left open from the call:
- Do you have any hard constraints on model family (open-source only) for security/compliance?
- Who on your end will sign the SOW (procurement contact)?

Thanks — happy to be flexible on the cohort if you want a smaller quick win first.

Best,
Marcus
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
attachments: [Redwood_TCO_Workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet), pilot-scope-pocketpay.pdf (pdf), pricing-deck-summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: Alan Chu <alan.chu@pocketpay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Reyes <samantha.reyes@pocketpay.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PocketPay: post-call TCO playbook and next steps

Appreciate the clear summary, Marcus — very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Pilot cohort: let's scope to 30k MAU (subset of the support summaries flow) rather than 50k to keep initial spend lower. If we see the expected savings we can expand.
- Logs: we'll provide 72 hours of anonymized logs by Monday. Security team requires data to be hashed; we'll coordinate with your solutions engineer.
- Model restrictions: security wants models vetted but open-source is preferred; need a short list of the model families you'll propose.
- Procurement: Catherine Li (catherine.li@pocketpay.com) will be the signatory for pilot SOW. I'll loop her in once we have a scope + workbook.

What would be most helpful now is a 2-page ROI snapshot that maps the batching/caching levers to dollar savings under a conservative scenario — finance will want to see that before any spend. If you can put that in the workbook as a top-sheet that'd be perfect.

Alan
Head of Platform — PocketPay

On Thu, Nov 5, 2026 at 15:12 Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for a productive call this morning — quick recap and clear next steps so we stay aligned...

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Alan Chu <alan.chu@pocketpay.com>, Samantha Reyes <samantha.reyes@pocketpay.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PocketPay: post-call TCO playbook and next steps — workbook attached

Alan / Samantha — attaching the workbook and pilot one-pager per our commitments. Top-sheet includes the conservative ROI snapshot you requested. Highlights below:

Attachment highlights:
- Redwood_TCO_Workbook.xlsx: conservative case assumes 15% token reduction via caching + 10% from batching = ~23% net savings; shows pilot spend at $28k for 6 weeks at 30k MAU.
- pilot-scope-pocketpay.pdf: instrumentation checklist (token-level traces, latency p95/p50, KV cache hit-rate), pilot entry/exit criteria, and estimated infra lead time (7 business days).
- pricing-deck-summary.pdf: two pricing options — hosted consumption pilot (no commit) and Dedicated pilot (1-month commit) with a step-down discount at month 3 if you commit to Reserved capacity.

Quick answers to open Qs:
- Model families: we'll prioritize Llama-3 family + a quantized variant for background embedding/rerank. We'll include a one-page security note for each model variant.
- SOW signatory: once you confirm Catherine's email I'll loop legal and share a draft SOW scoped to the 6-week pilot.

Proposed time to review workbook: Tue, Nov 9 at 11:00 AM PT — 30 minutes to walk the conservative scenario and instrumentation asks. If that works for Catherine I'll send a calendar invite and add Grace for ops checklist.

If you want a smaller immediate win, we can run a 2-week micro-pilot focused only on caching the top 10 intents (estimated spend $9k) to prove cache hit-rate and token reduction.

Regards,
Marcus
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
attachments: [Redwood_TCO_Workbook.xlsx, pilot-scope-pocketpay.pdf, pricing-deck-summary.pdf]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: PocketPay: post-call TCO playbook and next steps — quick ops notes

Alan — small ops notes from my side:
- We'll need a point person with infra access who can provide the anonymized request traces and help validate KV key patterns.
- Redwood will stand up tracing hooks and a token-cost dashboard; we typically send a read-only link for your finance to review.
- Onboarding ETA: once SOW is signed we can provision pilot infra in 5 business days.

I'll add Catherine on the next email thread once Marcus confirms the doc final. Looking forward to the sync on Tue.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
